findings.title: Unauthenticated WhatsApp webhook POST accepts forged Meta payloads without signature verification
findings.attacker: Any unauthenticated remote user on the internet
findings.controlled_input: Arbitrary JSON mimicking Meta entry[].changes[].value.messages[] (from, text.body, metadata.phone_number_id)
findings.attack_path: POST handler reads body with no X-Hub-Signature-256 check, calls createServiceRoleClient(), resolves clinic by phone_number_id or single-integration fallback, inserts inbound messages, and triggers chatbot routing, AI debounce, and sendChatbotReply outbound WhatsApp.
findings.impact: Inject fake patient conversations, force outbound WhatsApp replies to attacker numbers, trigger OpenAI/virtual-assistant cost abuse, and manipulate routing/handoff state.
findings.evidence: app/api/integrations/whatsapp/webhook/route.ts POST handler (lines 47-428) processes JSON with service role and never validates X-Hub-Signature-256; duplicate unsigned handler at app/api/whatsapp/webhook/route.ts; grep shows only Stripe webhook verifies signatures under app/api.

findings.title: Unauthenticated replay of automatic message sends via process-public-form-event
findings.attacker: Anyone who obtains a form_instance_id from public form submit network traffic
findings.controlled_input: form_instance_id UUID in POST JSON body
findings.attack_path: Unauthenticated POST uses service role to query event_timeline where status=pending, calls runAutoSendForEvent -> executeSendForEvent -> processMessageEvent/processEventByIdForPublicForm without checking sent_channels; event status stays pending after send.
findings.impact: Unlimited duplicate emails and WhatsApp messages to real patients; harassment, deliverability damage, and messaging cost abuse.
findings.evidence: app/api/process-public-form-event/route.ts has no auth; lib/event-send-logic-server.ts executeSendForEvent does not skip channels already in sent_channels; lib/message-processor.ts line 1216 keeps event status pending after send; form_instance_id exposed client-side in app/f/public/[token]/formulario-publico-preenchimento.tsx lines 127-130.

findings.title: Default Meta webhook verify token enables webhook hijack when env var is unset
findings.attacker: Anyone who knows the public webhook URL documented in code and Meta config
findings.controlled_input: hub.verify_token=flowmedi-verify during Meta subscription GET handshake
findings.attack_path: GET handler accepts verify token from hardcoded fallback META_WHATSAPP_WEBHOOK_VERIFY_TOKEN or flowmedi-verify and returns hub.challenge, allowing attacker to complete Meta webhook registration before legitimate operator.
findings.impact: Intercept or block real WhatsApp inbound traffic; combined with unsigned POST enables full message pipeline control.
findings.evidence: app/api/whatsapp/webhook/route.ts line 24 and app/api/integrations/whatsapp/webhook/route.ts line 24 both use process.env.META_WHATSAPP_WEBHOOK_VERIFY_TOKEN || flowmedi-verify; GET handler returns challenge when token matches (lines 31-38).

findings.title: Stored XSS in clinic staff event email preview via unescaped template variables
findings.attacker: Public user submitting a booking or public form with malicious field values
findings.controlled_input: Patient full_name, email, or form submitter fields containing HTML/JS payloads without spaces to bypass extractFirstName on nome_paciente variable
findings.attack_path: Malicious value stored via public booking endpoint -> getMessagePreview builds context -> replaceVariables inserts raw values without HTML escaping -> dangerouslySetInnerHTML in eventos-client.tsx renders preview when clinic staff views event.
findings.impact: JavaScript execution in authenticated clinic staff browser session (session theft, actions-as-victim).
findings.evidence: lib/message-variables.ts replaceVariables (lines 215-226) performs unescaped string substitution; app/dashboard/eventos/eventos-client.tsx line 1077 uses dangerouslySetInnerHTML on item.body; public input accepted at app/api/public/booking/[slug]/appointments/route.ts line 57.

findings.title: Public Supabase storage buckets expose clinical media and sequential financial PDFs
findings.attacker: Anyone with a leaked or guessed storage URL
findings.controlled_input: N/A (design flaw); receipt paths use sequential REC-year-seq numbering under clinicId/year/
findings.attack_path: Buckets receipts and quotes created with public=true; getPublicUrl returns permanently accessible URLs; one leaked URL reveals clinicId enabling enumeration of sequential receipt PDFs; whatsapp-media bucket is also public for any holder of media URL.
findings.impact: Unauthorized access to financial receipts/quotes and clinical WhatsApp media containing PHI.
findings.evidence: supabase/migration-journey-tools-events.sql lines 84-89 sets receipts and quotes buckets public; app/dashboard/financeiro/receipt-actions.ts line 293 uses sequential REC-year-seq paths; supabase/migration-whatsapp-media-bucket.sql creates public read policy for whatsapp-media.
